transcript.text: Thank you all for being here. As we know, Grandfather's grandfather clock is currently running in my hallway, and our family wants it to go to a relative's home rather than be sold or discarded. Before I make any final decision about who will receive the clock, where it will be placed, the move itself, any servicing it might need, and the chime settings, I want to hear from each of you. So I'll go around the room -- please share anything you think should shape this plan. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to share something. While going through Grandfather's papers, I found a signed estate note stating that the clock is to go to Rosa, the youngest grandchild. I haven't mentioned this to anyone until now, but I think the group needs to know.

transcript.text: I want to share something Rosa told me when we discussed the move. Her townhouse stairwell is 78 centimeters wide, but the clock case is 82 centimeters wide, so the clock can't be taken upstairs. If it goes to Rosa, it would have to stand in her ground-floor dining room rather than in an upstairs room.
